title: The action of $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ is transitive
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,F)$ be a Galois category [def-galois-category], $G=\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ and $X$ a connected object [def-galois-connected-object]. Then $G$ acts transitively on $F(X)$.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of isomorphism classes of Galois objects, choose a representative $X_i$ and an element $\gamma_i\in F(X_i)$ for each $i$. For $i,i'\in I$ write $i\ge i'$ when there is a morphism $f_{ii'}:X_i\to X_{i'}$; since $X_{i'}$ is Galois, post-compose with an automorphism of $X_{i'}$ so that $F(f_{ii'})(\gamma_i)=\gamma_{i'}$. This normalized morphism is unique by clause (5) of [lem-galois-axioms]. The set $I$ is directed: for $i_1,i_2$, take a connected component of $X_{i_1}\times X_{i_2}$ and apply [lem-galois-object-exists] to obtain a Galois object mapping to that component, hence to both factors.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN3, proof, first paragraph (lines 542-555)

proof.text: Define $F'(Y)=\varinjlim_{i\in I}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(X_i,Y)$ using the transition maps given by the normalized $f_{ii'}$, and define $t_Y:F'(Y)\to F(Y)$ by $[u:X_i\to Y]\mapsto F(u)(\gamma_i)$. If two representatives have the same image, choose a common upper index $k$; the two resulting maps $X_k\to Y$ agree on $\gamma_k$, hence are equal by clause (5) of [lem-galois-axioms], so $t_Y$ is injective. For surjectivity, decompose $Y$ into connected components using the Galois-category axiom and choose the component containing a given element of $F(Y)$. For a connected component $Y_0$, [lem-galois-object-exists] gives a Galois object $Z\to Y_0$; surjectivity of $F(Z)\to F(Y_0)$ follows from clauses (2) and (4) of [lem-galois-axioms]. After identifying $Z$ with some $X_i$, the transitivity in clause (6) of [lem-galois-axioms] lets us choose the identification so that $\gamma_i$ maps to the prescribed lift. Thus $t:F'\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ naturally.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN3, proof, paragraph beginning 'We claim that the functor F is isomorphic' (lines 557-580)

proof.text: Put $A_i=\operatorname{Aut}(X_i)$. For $i\ge i'$ and $a\in A_i$, clause (6) of [lem-galois-axioms] gives the unique $h_{ii'}(a)\in A_{i'}$ whose value on $\gamma_{i'}$ is $F(f_{ii'}a)(\gamma_i)$; clause (5) then gives $f_{ii'}a=h_{ii'}(a)f_{ii'}$. Uniqueness makes the $h_{ii'}$ compatible homomorphisms. They are surjective: for $b\in A_{i'}$, choose $x\in F(X_i)$ with $F(f_{ii'})(x)=F(b)(\gamma_{i'})$ (clauses (2) and (4)); by the Galois transitivity in clause (6), choose $a\in A_i$ with $F(a)(\gamma_i)=x$, and clause (5) gives $h_{ii'}(a)=b$. Let $A=\varprojlim_i A_i$. The groups $A_i$ are finite and nonempty, and the transition maps are surjective, so [lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective] makes every projection $A\to A_i$ surjective. An element $(a_i)_i\in A$ acts on $F'$ by precomposition, $[u:X_i\to Y]\mapsto[u a_i:X_i\to Y]$; compatibility of the $a_i$ makes this well-defined, and composition gives a homomorphism $A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Aut}(F')=\operatorname{Aut}(F)$. Since each $A\to A_i$ is surjective and $A_i$ acts transitively on $F(X_i)$ by clause (6), the induced $G$-action is transitive on every $F(X_i)$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN3, proof, paragraphs beginning 'Set A_i' and 'Since elements of A act' (lines 582-607), with Categories Lemma 086J for inverse-limit projections

proof.text: For the original connected object $X$, [lem-galois-object-exists] supplies a Galois object $X_i$ and a morphism $q:X_i\to X$. This is an epimorphism because both objects are connected, and $F(q)$ is therefore surjective by clauses (2) and (4) of [lem-galois-axioms]. Given $x,x'\in F(X)$, choose lifts $y,y'\in F(X_i)$. Transitivity on $F(X_i)$ gives $g\in G$ with $g(y)=y'$. Naturality of $g$ with respect to $q$ gives $g(x)=F(q)(g(y))=F(q)(y')=x'$, proving transitivity on $F(X)$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN3, proof, final sentence (lines 607-609), with Lemma 0BN2 for domination and Lemma 0BN0 clauses (2),(4)

proof_origin.place: Fundamental Groups of Schemes, Lemma 0BN3 (label lemma-tame), proof

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned split after checking that Mathlib's FiberFunctor.isPretransitive_of_isConnected is only a candidate for the Stacks 0BMY notion. The proof now follows Stacks Lemma 0BN3 (label lemma-tame) in four steps: the directed system of normalized Galois objects, the colimit description of the fibre functor, the compatible inverse system of finite automorphism groups and its induced Aut(F) action, and descent of transitivity along a Galois cover of the given connected object. The nontrivial finite inverse-limit projection fact is isolated as lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective, with its Stacks 086J source and Mathlib searches. The previous unsupported Mathlib-leaf interpretation and the unused profiniteness dependency were removed.
split_report.blueprint: The blueprint paragraph is realized in order: its directed system and common upper bounds are step 1; its colimit identification is step 2; its A_i, inverse limit, surjective projections and A^op -> Aut(F) action are step 3; and its final domination/transitivity argument is step 4.
